stick.hat.trim.name: Hat (hardware trim in standalone mode)
stick.hat.trim.note: hat cap on top of the grip

stick.trigger.name: Trigger
stick.trigger.note: index trigger below the head (photo-left side of the grip)

stick.gimbal.name: Stick (roll / pitch)
stick.gimbal.note: shaft exit at the top of the boot

stick.button.thumb.1.name: Red button (left of the hat)
stick.button.thumb.1.note: red button (photo left of the hat)

stick.button.thumb.2.name: Green button (right of the hat)
stick.button.thumb.2.note: green button (photo right of the hat)

source: JoyPro curated on the maker's photo (2026-10-11), the CLS-E MK II base with the BRUNNER Jet grip seen from the front left, slightly from above; hat on top with a red button (photo left) and a green button (photo right), index trigger sticking out below the head on the photo-left side
mappingSource: catalog brunner.json (quick install guide https://shop.brunner-simulation.ch/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/20240417_BRUNNER_QuickInstallGuide_CLS-E-MKII-joystick_V1.0.pdf, fact sheet https://shop.brunner-simulation.ch/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/20240304_Brunner_FactSheet_CLS-E-MKII-Joystick.pdf, product page https://brunner-innovation.swiss/product/brunner-jet/): USB X = roll, Y = pitch; grip controls named by the product photo (red button, green button, hat, trigger), their button numbers are not published
note: Parts are identified by colour/shape (red and green buttons, hat, trigger), so which part is which control is certain; the DirectInput button numbers are not published by Brunner. In standalone mode (no CLS2Sim) the hat is hardware trim.
